ground_truth.description: When an operator is slashed, the reward distribution formula doesn't correctly adjust proportions for remaining operators.
ground_truth.root_cause: When an operator is slashed, the reward distribution formula doesn't correctly adjust proportions for remaining operators.
ground_truth.fix_description: Recompute reward proportions dynamically when slashing occurs.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The checkpoint function incorrectly updates the effectiveBond when the year changes and inflation decreases. When incentives[4] < curMaxBond (inflation decreases), the code reduces effectiveBond by the difference. However, this subtraction happens AFTER effectiveBond has already been credited with curMaxBond at the start of the epoch. This double-counting can make effectiveBond negative (underflow to uint96 max) when bond programs have consumed more than the new reduced cap.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Wait for year boundary where inflation decreases (year 2→3 or 9→10). 2. Before checkpoint, bond programs consume most of effectiveBond. 3. When checkpoint runs with incentives[4] < curMaxBond, effectiveBond gets reduced further. 4. If effectiveBond < (curMaxBond - incentives[4]), subtraction underflows to ~uint96.max. 5. Subsequent bond programs can mint excessive OLAS due to inflated effectiveBond.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Track effectiveBond credit separately from actual bond consumption. Before adjusting for year change, subtract actual bond consumption from effectiveBond, then apply the maxBond adjustment: uint256 consumedBond = oldMaxBond - effectiveBond; effectiveBond = incentives[4] - min(consumedBond, incentives[4]);

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract has a critical flaw in the checkpoint function's effectiveBond adjustment logic during year transitions with decreasing inflation. This can lead to underflow and excessive OLAS minting. Other functions appear secure with proper access controls and validation. The vulnerability is exploitable during specific year boundaries and requires careful timing but doesn't need admin compromise.
